## Finding: Missing Agent Context (`crime_00017`)

The scan confirms the repo ships **no agent-readable instruction files**:

- No `AGENTS.md` at repo root
- No `CLAUDE.md` at repo root
- No `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- No `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- `package.json` declares `tsup` / `tsup-node` bins with no discoverability surface

Severity: **medium**, confidence **0.9**, agent_risk **0.53**.

## Consequence for future agent work

Agents loading this repo cold have no canonical place to learn:
- Which commands run the build, tests, typecheck, lint
- Workspace layout conventions (this is a monorepo-style tree with `src/esbuild/`, `src/rollup/`, `src/plugins/` — agents will guess at boundaries)
- Which files are load-bearing (the scan flags `src/plugin.ts` fan-in 10, `src/utils.ts` fan-in 18, `src/index.ts` fan-out 17 — none of which is obvious without reading)
- Safety rules / what not to touch

The downstream effect is confident-but-wrong edits: an agent will pick a plausible entry point, miss the actual build command, and ship a PR that doesn't even run locally. With 8 `large_function` highs already in the repo (`build` at 293 lines, `runEsbuild` at 237, `main` at 153), the surface area for mis-edits is large.

## Minimal `AGENTS.md` skeleton

Drop this at the repo root — it clears the finding and gives a cold-start agent the orientation it needs:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

## What this is
tsup — TypeScript bundler powered by esbuild. Ships a CLI (`tsup`, `tsup-node`).

## Commands
- Install:        pnpm install
- Build:          pnpm build
- Typecheck:      pnpm typecheck
- Test:           pnpm test
- Lint / format:  pnpm lint

Run the full check before opening a PR.

## Layout
- `src/index.ts`        — public entry: `build()`, `normalizeOptions()`, watcher
- `src/cli-main.ts`     — CLI argument parsing → `build()`
- `src/esbuild/`        — esbuild orchestration + plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`,
  `src/rollup/`         — rollup pipeline for .d.ts bundling
- `src/plugins/`        — first-party tsup plugins (terser, swc-target, cjs-splitting)
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin runtime / lifecycle (load-bearing: 10 importers)
- `src/utils.ts`        — shared helpers (load-bearing: 18 importers)
- `test/`               — Vitest suite; `test/utils.ts` is shared harness

## Load-bearing files (touch with care)
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin hook surface, 29-importer blast radius
- `src/utils.ts`        — used by ~everything; prefer adding new helpers over editing
- `src/index.ts`        — orchestrator; favor extracting helpers over inlining

## Conventions
- TypeScript, strict mode. No `any` without justification.
- Async I/O in domain code (no `*Sync` in hot paths).
- Prefix booleans with `is` / `has` / `should` / `can`.
- Don't read wall time directly in domain code — accept a clock if you need `now()`.
- Tests must assert observable behaviour, not just run setup. `expect(...).toBeDefined()` is not enough.

## Out of scope for most PRs
- Changing the public `Options` shape (breaks downstream tsup users).
- Reshaping `src/plugin.ts`'s exported types (29 importers).
```

That skeleton resolves `crime_00017` (presence check) and pre-empts several of the other findings agents would otherwise re-discover the hard way (sync I/O, booleans, weak tests, load-bearing files).
